item.title: Region Settings
item.description:
Get Region Settings #

Returns the settings configured for the region.

Requests # 

GET /_cluster/_region/<region_id>/settings

Path Parameters #

  • region_id
    (Required, String) The UUID of the region you want to query. A special ID _local can be specified to query the state of the region that handles this request.

Query Parameters #

  • include_defaults
    (Optional, Boolean) If true, returns all default region settings. Defaults to false.

  • flat_settings
    (Optional, Boolean) If true, returns settings in flat format. Defaults to false.

item.title: Node Settings
item.description: Node settings are runtime-tunable knobs that apply to a single node. Every setting is a transient override over the persistent pizza.yml value (or the built-in default): a change takes effect immediately via PUT and disappears at restart — set the same key in the yml for a persistent value. This is the node-scope sibling of the Raft-replicated Region Settings: routing policy is cluster-wide, while log verbosity, search lane budgets and trash retention are per-node concerns.

item.title: Configuration file reference
item.description:
Configuration file reference #

pizza.yml (the default lookup path, override with -c/--config <file>) is read once at startup. Unknown keys are rejected — the node refuses to start on a typo, and on a key that was renamed in an upgrade. Individual keys can be overridden per launch with pizza -E <key>=<value> (repeatable; values parse as YAML, e.g. -E node.network.binding=127.0.0.1:12200).

Secret values #

API keys and tokens do not have to live in the file. Any string value may reference an environment variable, resolved at startup:

item.title: Environment variables
item.description:
Environment variables #

Most tuning lives in pizza.yml (see the configuration file reference) or the runtime settings APIs. The PIZZA_* environment variables below are escape hatches — mostly for benchmarking, diagnostics and crash-safety research; prefer the config file or the settings APIs for anything you want to keep.

Operational knobs #

Variable Default Description
PIZZA_FLUSH_CONCURRENCY unset Overrides node.flush_concurrency (1..=16); beats the config file.
PIZZA_RECOVERY_TAIL_FLUSH unset 0/1 forces wal.local.recovery_tail_flush off/on, beating the config file.
PIZZA_RPC_TIMEOUT_SECS unset Deadline for cluster RPC calls (must be > 0).
PIZZA_COMPACTION_EVERY_TICKS unset Maintenance ticks (500 ms) between background compaction passes.
PIZZA_COMPACT_TIERS unset Restrict background compaction to specific tier patterns (diagnostics).
PIZZA_FLUSH_AFTER_IDLE_TICKS unset Idle-tail epoch flush override (same semantics as wal.local.epoch_flush_after_idle_ticks).
PIZZA_SEGMENT_SYNC unset off skips the per-segment fsync before WAL purge — the same behavior as wal.local.segment_durability: async, without a config change.
PIZZA_WAL_IO_URING unset Force WAL io_uring on/off (Linux), overriding auto-detection.
PIZZA_MAX_NODE_BUILDS unset Fallback for the epoch-build concurrency default (PUT /_node/_local/settings/epoch_build overrides it at runtime).
PIZZA_MERGE_POOL_THREADS unset Size of the dedicated compaction merge thread pool.
PIZZA_ROUTE_CACHE unset Routing-table cache diagnostics/tuning.
PIZZA_BUILD_BUF_POOL_MB unset Build-buffer pool size in MiB.

Watchdog #

Variable Default Description
PIZZA_RSS_WATCHDOG unset Enable the RSS watchdog (0 explicitly disables it).
PIZZA_RSS_SOFT_MB 60% of MemTotal Soft RSS threshold (MiB) — sheds load, logs.
PIZZA_RSS_HARD_MB 75% of MemTotal Hard RSS threshold (MiB) — aborts the process.

Diagnostics and profiling #

Off by default; presence enables.

item.title: AI Services
item.description: AI services are the external, OpenAI-compatible model endpoints behind server-side inference — schema-driven text→vector derivation, text vector queries, the semantic query and the /_embedding API on the embedding side, and the POST /_chat generation facade on the other. Every service speaks the OpenAI wire format: the embeddings API (POST {url} with {"model", "input": [...]} and a bearer key), and — once it lists generation models — the chat-completions API at its chat_url.

item.title: Keystore
item.description:
Keystore #

The keystore is a node-local file of secrets referenced from pizza.yml — API keys and tokens never have to live in the config file itself. Entries resolve through ${keystore:NAME} references:

node:
 embedding:
 endpoints:
 - name: openai
 url: https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings
 api_key: ${keystore:openai}

The file is <config dir>/keystore.json — next to the config file it serves, so one instance per config (multi-instance hosts keep separate keystores) and it never enters the data directory’s lifecycle. It is written 0600 and replaced atomically; entries never enter cluster metadata, raft logs, or API responses — views answer with a masked hint only (sk-…4f2a).
